business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K business description and the 10-Q MD&A overview.
business_model.claim: Pagaya runs an AI-powered network that connects financial institutions and their customers with investors. Its Partners are lenders, and its investors fund the assets those lenders originate.
quotes: We have built and continue to enhance a network connecting financial institutions and their customers with investors, which is designed to facilitate greater access to financial products and services for consumers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 product table and competitive-strengths list.
business_model.claim: It sells a suite of lender-facing products, including Decline Monetization, Dual Look, First Look, Affiliate Optimizer Engine, Direct Marketing Engine and FastPass. These cover personal loans, auto loans and point-of-sale, and the business also includes single-family rental. The 10-K cites 30+ U.S. lenders.
quotes: Our business began in personal loans and has expanded to auto loans, point-of-sale and single-family rental
expansion to 30+ U.S. lenders

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A economic-model sections.
business_model.claim: Revenue is primarily driven by Network Volume. Revenue from fees combines network AI fees and contract fees. Network AI fees split into AI integration fees and capital markets execution fees. Contract fees are management, performance and similar fees. Pagaya also earns interest income and investment income.
quotes: revenues are primarily derived from Network Volume
Revenue from fees is comprised of network AI fees and contract fees.

business_model.basis: Taken directly from the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Fee revenue is the bulk of income. Revenue from fees was 1,026,785 for the nine months ended Sep. 30, 2026, against 940,305 a year earlier, within total revenue and other income of 1,095,478 (table in thousands). Third-quarter revenue from fees was 362,155 against 339,887.

business_model.basis: Stated in footnote 1 to the 10-Q income statement. The link to dependence on vehicle funding is inferred.
business_model.claim: A large share of fee revenue comes from related parties, meaning ABS securitization trusts and investment funds that Pagaya manages or sponsors. Related-party revenues were $627.5 million for the nine months ended Sep. 30, 2026, against $473.7 million a year earlier.
quotes: $627.5 million and $473.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A, the Q3 earnings release and the 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Network Volume drives both revenue and production costs. Third-quarter Network Volume was $3.6 billion, up 29%. Production costs, which compensate Partners for acquiring and originating assets, were 215,701 in the quarter against 200,574 a year earlier (table in thousands). Revenue from fees less production costs (FRLPC) was $146 million, or 4.1% of Network Volume.
quotes: the amount and growth of our Production Costs are highly correlated to Network Volume

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 earnings release and the 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Cost of capital is a key driver of fee margin. FRLPC as a share of volume contracted by 91 basis points year over year to 4.1%, which the company attributes to higher benchmark rates. The 10-Q says the higher cost of capital has required adjustments to conversion ratios to meet investor return expectations.
quotes: driven by the short-term impact of higher benchmark rates
the cost of capital has risen, necessitating adjustments in conversion ratios to meet investor return expectations

business_model.basis: Taken directly from the 10-Q income statement. The conclusion that production costs are the largest line is inferred from the table.

The other cost lines are small by comparison: technology, data and product development 17,352, sales and marketing 9,514, and general and administrative 35,377.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 shareholder letter within the 8-K.
